facts.statement: The first Shunosaurus fossil, a partial skeleton, was discovered in 1977 by students excavating a road bank at Dashanpu in Sichuan.
facts.quote: The first fossil of Shunosaurus, a partial skeleton, was discovered in 1977 by a group of students, practising paleontological excavation at a road bank at Dashanpu, Zigong, Sichuan.

facts.statement: The genus and species Shunosaurus lii were formally described by Dong Zhiming, Zhou Shiwu, and Zhang Yihong in 1983.
facts.quote: The new genus and species Shunosaurus lii were described and named based on this specimen by Dong Zhiming, Zhou Shiwu and Zhang Yihong in 1983.

facts.statement: Shunosaurus lived in Sichuan Province, China, during the Late Jurassic (Oxfordian) from 161 to 157 million years ago.
facts.quote: Shunosaurus () is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from Late Jurassic (Oxfordian) beds in Sichuan Province in China, from 161 to 157 Million years ago.

facts.statement: Initial estimates placed Shunosaurus at 11 meters long, but later more complete fossils suggested a somewhat smaller size.
facts.quote: Shunosaurus was first estimated to be 11 m long; later and more complete finds indicated a somewhat smaller size.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated Shunosaurus to be 9.5 meters long and weigh 3 metric tons.
facts.quote: In 2010 Gregory S. Paul estimated the length at 9.5 m, the weight at 3 MT.

facts.statement: Shunosaurus had a very short neck for a sauropod, comparable to members of the family Dicraeosauridae.
facts.quote: Shunosaurus was very short-necked for a sauropod, comparable to certain members of Dicraeosauridae.

facts.statement: The upper and lower jaws of Shunosaurus were strongly curved upwards, functioning like a pair of garden shears.
facts.quote: The upper and lower jaws were strongly curved upwards, allowing them to function as a pair of garden shears.

facts.statement: Shunosaurus possessed fairly robust but elongated teeth with a crown length of up to 8 centimeters.
facts.quote: The teeth were fairly robust but elongated with a crown length of up to 8 cm.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the tail club of Shunosaurus was probably used to fend off predators.
facts.quote: The club was probably used to fend off predators.

facts.statement: The neck length of Shunosaurus indicates it was a low browser.
facts.quote: Its neck length indicates that Shunosaurus was a low browser.

facts.statement: Shunosaurus accounts for 90% of the fossils in the Dashanpu fauna, indicating it was a dominant or common member of its environment.
facts.quote: Shunosaurus accounts for 90% of the fossils found in the Dashanpu fauna, showing it was a dominant and/ or common member of its habitat and environment.

facts.statement: Shunosaurus was originally classified as a member of Cetiosaurinae, but in 1992 it was assigned to Shunosaurinae within Cetiosauridae.
facts.quote: Shunosaurus was originally classified as a member of the Cetiosaurinae; in 1992 Dong assigned it to Shunosaurinae within the Cetiosauridae.

facts.statement: Cladistic analyses have produced conflicting results regarding Shunosaurus' classification, with some studies placing it in Euhelopodidae and others indicating a basal position within Eusauropoda.
facts.quote: Cladistic analyses have rendered conflicting results. In 1995 Paul Upchurch published a study in which Shunosaurus belonged to the Euhelopodidae together with other Jurassic Chinese sauropods. However, an analysis by Jeffrey Wilson in 2002 indicated it had a very basal position within the Eusauropoda.

facts.statement: Due to compressed or disarticulated skulls, interpretations of Shunosaurus' head form have varied from broad and short to extremely narrow and pointed.
facts.quote: The skulls found are mostly compressed or disarticulated and the interpretation of the head form has varied from broad, short and deep to extremely narrow and pointed.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Shunosaurus may have used its long thumb claw as a weapon.
facts.quote: También pudo haber usado como arma la garra larga ubicada en el dedo pulgar.

facts.statement: Shunosaurus is a genus of cetiosaurid sauropods that lived in Asia during the Late and Middle Jurassic, approximately between 165 and 159 million years ago.
facts.quote: Shunosaurus ("lagarto de Shu") un género representado por dos especies conocidas, y posiblemente una tercera, de dinosaurios saurópodos cetiosáuridos que vivierón a finales y mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 165 a 159 millones de años, desde el Bathoniense al Oxfordiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: Shuosaurus Chow, 1979 is a synonym for the genus Shunosaurus.
facts.quote: synonyms: Shuosaurus Chow, 1979

facts.statement: The first fossil of Shunosaurus was discovered in 1977 by a group of students practicing paleontological excavations on the side of a road.
facts.quote: El primer fósil de Shunosaurus fue descubierto en 1977 por un grupo de estudiantes que practicaban excavaciones paleontológicas en la orilla de una carretera.

facts.statement: The type species, Shunosaurus lii, was described and named by Dong Zhiming, Zhou Shiwu, and Zhang Yihong in 1983.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, Shunosaurus lii, fue descrita y nombrada por Dong Zhiming , Zhou Shiwu y Zhang Yihong en 1983.

facts.statement: The holotype, IVPP V.9065, was collected from the Lower Xiashaximiao Formation near Dashanpu, Zigong.
facts.quote: El holotipo, IVPP V.9065, fue recolectado de la Formación Xiashaximiao Inferior cerca de Dashanpu, Zigong.

facts.statement: More than twenty additional significant specimens were later discovered, including several complete or nearly complete skeletons and skulls, making Shunosaurus one of the best anatomically known sauropods with 94% of all skeletal elements identified.
facts.quote: Más tarde se descubrieron unos veinte especímenes importantes más, incluidos varios esqueletos, cráneos y juveniles completos o casi completos, haciendo de Shunosaurus uno de los saurópodos mejor conocidos anatómicamente, con el 94% de todos los elementos esqueléticos identificados.

facts.statement: In 2004, a partial semi-articulated specimen from Jiangyi town in Yuanmou County was described as the new species Shunosaurus jiangyiensis.
facts.quote: En 2004, un espécimen parcial semi-articulado del municipio de Jiangyi en el condado de Yuanmou fue descrito como la nueva especie Shunosaurus jiangyiensis.

facts.statement: The species was separated from Shunosaurus lii based on its unique pectoral girdle but was described as very similar to both Shunosaurus lii and Kunmingosaurus.
facts.quote: La especie se separó de Shunosaurus lii en función de su cintura pectoral única, pero se describió como muy similar tanto a Shunosaurus lii como a Kunmingosaurus.

facts.statement: The specimen of Shunosaurus jiangyiensis is found in the upper Middle Jurassic section of the Xiashaximiao Formation.
facts.quote: que se encuentra en la sección superior del Jurásico medio de la Formación Xiashaximiao.

facts.statement: Shunosaurus lived from the Aalenian to the Oxfordian stages, between 174.7 and 154.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aalenian to Oxfordian (174.7 to 154.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: Shunosaurus was originally classified as a member of Cetiosaurinae, but in 1992 Dong assigned it to Shunosaurinae within Cetiosauridae.
facts.quote: Shunosaurus fue originalmente clasificado como miembro de Cetiosaurinae, en 1992 Dong lo asignó a Shunosaurinae dentro de Cetiosauridae.

facts.statement: However, a 2002 analysis by Jeffrey Wilson indicated that Shunosaurus had a very basal position within Eusauropoda.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, un análisis de Jeffrey Wilson en 2002 indicó que tenía una posición muy básica dentro de Eusauropoda.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Shunosaurus is related to Rhoetosaurus from Queensland, Australia.
facts.quote: Shunosaurus quizás esté relacionado con Rhoetosaurus de Queensland en Australia.

facts.statement: Shunosaurus is classified as a member of the parent group Eusauropoda.
facts.quote: Parent group: Eusauropoda

facts.statement: Shunosaurus belongs to the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Shunosaurus shared its territory with other sauropods like Datousaurus, Omeisaurus, and Protognathosaurus, the possible ornithopod Xiaosaurus, the possible stegosaurian Huayangosaurus, and the theropod Gasosaurus.
facts.quote: Compartió el territorio con otros saurópodos como Datousaurus, Omeisaurus y Protognathosaurus, el posible ornitópodo Xiaosaurus y el posible estegosauriano Huayangosaurus y el terópodo Gasosaurus.

facts.statement: Since 1979, more than 10 complete or nearly complete skeletons of this dinosaur have been found, making it one of the best-known sauropods and representing 90% of the formation's fossils.
facts.quote: Desde 1979 se han encontrado más de 10 esqueletos de este dinosaurio, completos o casi completos, lo que lo hace uno de los mejores saurópodos conocidos y representa el 90 % de los fósiles de la formación.

facts.statement: The generic name Shunosaurus derives from "Shu", an ancient name for Sichuan.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico deriva de "Shu", un antiguo nombre de Sichuan.

facts.statement: The specific name honors Li Bing, the governor of Sichuan.
facts.quote: El nombre específico honra a Li Bing, gobernador de Sichuan en el .

facts.statement: Shunosaurus skeletons are exhibited at the Zigong Dinosaur Museum in Zigong, Sichuan province, and the Tianjin Natural History Museum.
facts.quote: Los esqueletos de Shunosaurus se exhiben en el Museo de Dinosaurios de Zigong en Zigong, provincia de Sichuan, y en el Museo de Historia Natural de Tianjin.
